items.corrected_text: A Reims low-emission-zone support document (its text is undated; the PDF file was created in April 2023) describes the Citura network as having one tram line with three park-and-rides connected to it (Neufchatel, Belges, Hopital Debre). It says the tram alone serves a third of the population of the territory, 27% of jobs and 75% of students. It adds that Champagne Parc Auto runs the Zebullo self-service e-bike scheme (120 bikes, 13 stations) and that Reims has more than 5,000 bicycle parking places. The latest events it dates are from September 2021 and it treats 2022 as still to come, so it seems to describe the position around late 2021; the operator's own 2026 page lists four park-and-ride sites, including Thillois.

items.corrected_text: A Caradisiac article published on 14 March 2023 reports that the city of Reims announced, in an official press release published the day before (a Monday), that it would not apply the planned January 2024 ban on Crit'Air 3 vehicles in its low-emission zone, which was pushed back to 2029. The stated reason was an average nitrogen dioxide level of 31 micrograms per cubic metre in the city centre in 2022, below the EU limit of 40 (41 in 2019).

items.corrected_text: A report published on 10 July 2023 on the L'infodurable site says Reims introduced its low-emission zone on 1 January 2023, barring diesel cars registered up to 31 December 2005 (Crit'Air 4). It adds that Reims had already imposed a moratorium on Crit'Air 3 vehicles in March, giving them until 2029. On the same day the government's new classification placed Reims in a 'zone de vigilance' this year, which lets it decide to suspend the next steps of its restriction calendar.

corrected_summary: Reims's paid city-centre garages are run by Champagne Parc Auto, a semi-public company owned mostly by the Grand Reims authority (48.59%) and the city (22.83%), under concession and lease contracts from Grand Reims. The authority's 2022 report counts 2,053 public spaces in five garages (Buirette, Cathedrale, Erlon, Gambetta, Hotel de Ville), and says the hourly prices in force in 2022 had not changed since July 2014 and subscription prices since January 2012; no later change was found. The network operator's page lists four park-and-ride sites on the tram and bus network, open around the clock, with exit by validated transit ticket. In 2023 the city announced, citing lower nitrogen dioxide in 2022, that the Crit'Air 3 ban in its low-emission zone, planned for January 2024, would be pushed back to 2029, and a report of July 2023 says the zone started on 1 January 2023 and that the government put Reims in a 'zone de vigilance'. On 21 May 2026 the Constitutional Council struck down the clauses that would have abolished low-emission zones nationally, without mentioning Reims. A commercial parking site, not confirmed by any official page, describes on-street parking as paid Monday to Saturday in four colour zones with a 25 euro post-parking charge. The official Grand Reims, Reims city and Citura websites blocked automated access, so the briefing is thin on current tariffs, the on-street regime, traffic-plan changes and new garage projects, and no utilisation figures or open-data parking feed were found.
